entries.question_title: Closed-loop buck converter voltage across C9
entries.key_topic: Steady-state voltage across feedback-network capacitor C9
entries.image_storage: Image not stored in GitHub. User keeps images in a separate Word document and uses caption in description.md.
entries.caption: Closed-loop buck converter feedback-network case study: the circuit asks for the steady-state voltage across capacitor C9, using the feedback divider R2 = 2 kΩ and R3 = 1 kΩ with βVref = 2.5 V; in steady state, C9 is open-circuit and its voltage is set by the output voltage and feedback-node voltage.
entries.asked_for: Voltage across capacitor C9 in volts
entries.method_summary: Use α=R3/(R2+R3)=1/3 and αVo=βVref=2.5 V, so Vo=7.5 V. In steady-state C9 is open-circuit; its lower terminal is at the feedback node 2.5 V and its upper terminal is at Vo, so VC9=7.5−2.5=5.00 V.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning: capacitors are open circuits in steady-state DC analysis
Circuit reasoning: feedback divider α = R3/(R2+R3)
Ideal buck relation Vo = δVdc used only as a consistency check

entries.question_title: Turn-on snubber inductor from MOSFET drain-current rise time
entries.key_topic: Using snubber inductance to control MOSFET drain-current slew rate at turn-on
entries.image_storage: Image not stored in GitHub. User keeps images in a separate Word document and uses caption in description.md.
entries.caption: Turn-on snubber sizing question: MOSFET switch with inductive load, Vdc = 187 V, fpwm = 5 kHz, duty d = 30 %, and load current IL = 5 A; the series snubber inductor Ls is chosen so the MOSFET drain current rises to IL in 1 µs, giving Ls = 37.40 µH.
entries.asked_for: Turn-on snubber inductance Ls in microhenries
entries.method_summary: Use vL = L di/dt. During the turn-on transient, Ls is treated as having approximately Vdc across it while MOSFET drain current rises from 0 A to IL, so Ls = Vdc × tr / IL = 187 × 1e-6 / 5 = 37.40 µH.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning: snubber inductor controls drain-current slew during MOSFET turn-on

entries.question_title: Buck-boost converter CCM peak-to-peak inductor current ripple
entries.key_topic: Peak-to-peak inductor current ripple in inverting buck-boost converter operating in CCM
entries.image_storage: Image not stored in GitHub. User keeps images in a separate Word document and uses caption in description.md.
entries.caption: Buck-boost converter CCM inductor-ripple question: Vdc = 35 V, |Vo| = 27 V, fpwm = 50 kHz, L = 344 µH, and C = 47 µF; using the CCM buck-boost duty ratio and Mode 1 inductor ramp gives a peak-to-peak inductor current ripple of ΔIL = 0.89 A.
entries.asked_for: Peak-to-peak inductor current ripple ΔIL in amperes
entries.method_summary: Use buck-boost CCM relation d = |Vo|/(Vdc + |Vo|) = 27/(35+27) = 0.4355. During Mode 1, vL = Vdc, so ΔIL = Vdc × d/(L × fpwm) = 35 × 0.4355/(344e−6 × 50e3) = 0.89 A.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning / volt-second balance: |Vo| = Vdc d/(1−d) for CCM buck-boost magnitude form

entries.question_title: Closed-loop buck converter Vdc from C2 voltage and PWM control
entries.subcategory: case studies / feedback-control / PWM duty calculation
entries.key_topic: Finding Vdc from feedback divider, compensation capacitor voltage, PWM comparator and ideal buck relation
entries.image_storage: Image not stored in GitHub. User keeps images in a separate Word document and uses caption in description.md.
entries.caption: Closed-loop buck converter feedback-control question: with R12 = 3 kΩ, R13 = 3 kΩ, βVref = 2.5 V, vsaw = 5 V, and vC2 = 0.5 V, the feedback divider gives Vo = 5.00 V and the PWM control voltage gives δ = 0.60, so the required input voltage is Vdc = 8.33 V.
entries.method_summary: Use α = R13/(R12+R13) = 0.5 and αVo = βVref = 2.5 V, so Vo = 5.00 V. The control voltage is u = βVref + vC2 = 3.0 V, giving duty δ = u/vsaw = 0.60. Then ideal buck relation Vo = δVdc gives Vdc = 5.00/0.60 = 8.33 V.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning: feedback divider α = R13/(R12+R13)
Circuit reasoning: closed-loop steady-state condition αVo = βVref
Circuit reasoning: PWM duty ratio δ = u/vsaw

entries.question_title: Closed-loop buck converter beta from feedback bias current
entries.key_topic: Finding beta from feedback-divider bias current and reference voltage
entries.image_storage: Image not stored in GitHub. User keeps images in a separate Word document and uses caption in description.md.
entries.caption: Closed-loop buck converter feedback-divider question: with bias current through R12 of 1 mA, R13 = 3 kΩ, and Vref = 7.79 V, the feedback node voltage is 3.00 V, so the required reference scaling factor is β = 0.39.
entries.method_summary: Use steady-state op-amp equality αVo = βVref. The feedback node voltage is αVo = IBIAS × R13 = 1 mA × 3 kΩ = 3.00 V. Therefore β = 3.00/7.79 = 0.39.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning: steady-state closed-loop condition αVo = βVref
Ohm's law: feedback node voltage across R13 equals IBIAS × R13
Derived equation: β = IBIAS R13 / Vref
